title: Infrastructure Orchestration with Terraform & Pulumi (PYTH_176_S1 to PYTH_176_S8)

slides.title: Pulumi Python Infrastructure as Code
slides.prompt: Pulumi lets developers define, deploy, and manage cloud infrastructure using pure Python code instead of static domain-specific languages.
slides.codeSnippet:
import pulumi
from pulumi_aws import s3

bucket = s3.Bucket('my-bucket')
pulumi.export('bucket_name', bucket.id)

slides.title: Exporting Pulumi Outputs
slides.prompt: Fill in the function used to output deployed infrastructure values at the end of a Pulumi execution.

slides.title: State Management in IaC
slides.prompt: Why is storing infrastructure state in a centralized backend (e.g., AWS S3 with locking) necessary?
options: To prevent concurrent deployments from corrupting cloud resources and track managed configurations
To automatically convert Python code into YAML template files
To reduce billing costs of provisioned virtual servers
To compile Python code into executable binary packages
slides.correctAnswer: To prevent concurrent deployments from corrupting cloud resources and track managed configurations

slides.title: Pulumi Resource Creation
slides.prompt: Fill in the module used to instantiate EC2 virtual servers using Pulumi in Python.
slides.codeSnippet:
from pulumi_aws import ec2

server = ec2.___('web-server', instance_type='t3.micro')

slides.title: Imperative vs Declarative IaC
slides.prompt: How does Pulumi handle resource updates during deployment execution?
options: It constructs a declarative dependency graph and computes diffs before executing changes
It destroys and recreates all cloud resources on every deployment run
It runs raw shell scripts sequentially on target instances via SSH
It sends manual REST API POST commands without tracking existing state
slides.correctAnswer: It constructs a declarative dependency graph and computes diffs before executing changes

slides.title: Pulumi Configuration Values
slides.prompt: Fill in the class used to retrieve configuration secrets or deployment parameters.

slides.title: Testing IaC Code in Python
slides.prompt: What major advantage does using Python for IaC (Pulumi/CDK) provide for automated testing?
options: Ability to write standard unit tests with Pytest using mocks without provisioning real infrastructure
Elimination of all cloud resource pricing during deployment runs
Automatic conversion of infrastructure code into mobile apps
Execution of infrastructure deploys directly inside browser runtimes
slides.correctAnswer: Ability to write standard unit tests with Pytest using mocks without provisioning real infrastructure
